reading: The proposal rewords one open question, q-conversion-settlement (E5, E9). It used to ask whether the Book 20 hands-to-draw conversion is a lasting settlement or a stage the finale must revisit. It would now ask whether the conversion reaches the shares the Mill Compact purchased. The instruction asks for exactly this, with no answer given and every other question and element unchanged (E1). The question the author is considering therefore shifts from how long the conversion lasts to whom it covers. The Compact settlement question and the lowland-debt question keep their wording (E14, E18).

concerns.title: Is the Book 20 conversion a lasting settlement or a stage?
concerns.earlier: Asked whether the conversion is a lasting settlement or a stage the finale must revisit (E5).
concerns.proposed: The proposed wording asks only whether the conversion reaches the Compact's purchased shares (E9); it does not mention lasting or provisional status.
concerns.reading: The settlement-or-stage dimension no longer appears in the question's wording. Whether it should be asked separately, or was deliberately set aside, is not shown. This reads the wording change only; it does not show that the concern has been abandoned.
counterevidence: The instruction says to change only the wording and not to decide the answer (E1), which does not say the earlier concern is dropped.
concerns.competing_reading: The author may regard settlement-or-stage as still implied, and treat the new question as a narrowing within it.

concerns.title: Scope of the conversion (who it covers)
concerns.earlier: The conversion was treated as one Book 20 event whose permanence was open (E5).
concerns.proposed: The conversion's reach over purchased shares becomes the open matter (E9).
concerns.reading: The question is still about the same conversion, but its function changes from a question of duration to a question of coverage. This links it to the Compact's purchased draw, which carries no return labour (E3).
concerns.competing_reading: Interpretation: the new wording may be a sharper form of the original concern, not a different concern.

concerns.title: Link between the conversion and the Compact settlement
concerns.reading: Reaching the Compact's shares ties q-conversion-settlement to q-compact-settlement and to q-other-1 (what lowland towns owe Ammen). The record shows that the discovery origin and the selected alternative considered all three questions together (E2, E3). The questions are separate in the Architecture, and the proposal leaves the other two untouched (E14, E18), so this is a new coupling the author may or may not want.

concerns.title: Compact settlement and lowland-debt questions stay as they were
concerns.reading: The wording of both questions is unchanged under the proposal, so they remain open and available to be answered independently.
counterevidence: An unchanged question can still gain a dependency from the reworded neighbour (E3).

prospective.text: Book 24, The Uncounted Crew, records a decision on this question by identity, and the proposal rewords the question. That is a recorded relationship, not a demonstrated contradiction. The decision text still speaks of lasting settlement or stage (E8), and whether Book 24 needs reconsidering is not shown.

Book 24 also records the Compact grain-labour question, whose wording is unchanged (E13). The proposed question may bear on how Oona's offer is read, but the record shows only that both are held in Book 24.

Speculative possibility: if later Books treat the conversion as reaching purchased shares, the Compact might owe an unreturned-hands balance that grain-labour could settle (E3). If it does not reach them, the conversion binds only households and the cost of counting may be sharper. Neither is established or chosen.

alternatives.title: Adopt the reach wording as the opened question
alternatives.summary: Speculative alternative: keep the proposal as worded, so q-conversion-settlement asks about reach. Keeps the Compact settlement and lowland-debt questions unchanged and open.
alternatives.gains: Opens the Compact coverage question directly, as the instruction asks, and decides nothing.
alternatives.costs: The settlement-or-stage question loses its place in the wording, and Book 24's recorded decision text no longer matches.
alternatives.next_investigation: Check whether Book 24 and Book 25 rely on the settlement-or-stage framing.

alternatives.title: Keep the original question and ask reach separately
alternatives.summary: Speculative alternative: leave q-conversion-settlement as it was and describe reach as a distinct question, which is not given an identity here. It keeps q-conversion-settlement and q-compact-settlement.
alternatives.gains: Keeps both the settlement-or-stage and the reach concerns visible, and leaves Book 24's decision text matching.
alternatives.costs: Adds an open question, and the author must decide whether it needs its own place.
alternatives.next_investigation: Decide whether reach is independent of lasting-or-stage by testing a Book 24 scene both ways.

alternatives.title: Treat conversion reach and Compact settlement together
alternatives.summary: Speculative alternative: ask the conversion's reach and the Compact's settlement as one linked matter, since the selected alternative and discovery origin considered them together (E2, E3).
alternatives.gains: Reflects the dependency the record already shows and may reduce contradictory answers.
alternatives.costs: Merges three questions, which could force an answer to one to settle the others early.
alternatives.next_investigation: List which answers to one question would constrain the others, without choosing any.

alternatives.title: Hold the baseline wording until Book 25 is read
alternatives.summary: Speculative alternative: keep the baseline wording for now. Book 25 was listed by title only and was not read for decisions.
alternatives.gains: Avoids rewording on partial coverage of the Working Books.
alternatives.costs: Leaves the Compact coverage question unopened and delays the idea in the instruction.
alternatives.next_investigation: Read Book 25's decisions on these questions, then reconsider.
